1.explanation: The TableToolbarSearch component is the function that renders the search container <div> with role="searchbox". It never applies an aria-label (or aria-labelledby) on that div, so screen readers have no accessible name for the searchbox. Fixing this requires updating TableToolbarSearch to pass the labelText (or a translation key) through to the container via aria-label or aria-labelledby.
1.bug_scenario: In the DataTable example, the toolbar’s search box container is rendered as a <div> with role="searchbox" but no aria-label or aria-labelledby attribute. As a result, JAWS cannot identify it and reads it as “? Edit” or “Unlabeled# Edit.”

2.explanation: The missing accessible name on the <div role="searchbox"> is defined inside the TableToolbarSearch component. This function renders the wrapper div (with role="searchbox") and passes through labelText or a default string from translateWithId, but never applies it as aria-label on the container. To fix the issue, the TableToolbarSearch component’s render logic must be updated to add an aria-label (or aria-labelledby) to that wrapping <div>, using the existing labelText prop or translateWithId output. The translateWithId function defines the default text ("Filter table") and is the source for the label, so it is also part of the changes to ensure the right label is applied.
2.bug_scenario: In the DataTable example, the toolbar’s search input is wrapped in a <div role="searchbox"> container that has no aria-label or aria-labelledby attribute. When JAWS encounters this searchbox region, it reads it as an unlabeled “Edit” field (e.g. “? Edit” or “Unlabeled# Edit”), making the control inaccessible.
